subject: Post-call: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Hi Tom —

Quick recap from our call this morning and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of asked items:
- Latency targets: p50/p95 for single-turn generation, and tail targets for streaming (we discussed p95 <= 200ms for short prompts, p95 <= 400ms for longer).
- Throughput / concurrency: expected sustained qps and peak concurrency (you mentioned ~300 qps sustained and spikes to 1k qps).
- Streaming: support for chunked streaming with per-token latency <= 50ms where possible, and graceful fallback to non-streaming if degraded.
- Regional routing / residency: multi-region requirement (US + EU) with APAC for future rollout; EU data residency for EU-sourced requests and audit traceability.

Next steps / owners:
1) I will share our SLO matrix and a regional routing sketch (attached). (owner: me)
2) Tom to confirm target qps by region and any session affinity requirements. (owner: Finova)
3) If residency requires EU-only data plane for EU requests, we’ll loop infra/solutions to validate. (cc: Aditya)
4) Procurement: once we lock targets we can align on Dedicated vs Hosted sizing and draft a mutual action plan.

Attachments: redwood-slos-matrix.pdf (SLO table), regional-routing-design.drawio (sketch)

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if useful.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Tom Li <tom.li@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: target p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms for short completion paths (~<256 tokens). For streaming user experiences we need token-level latencies that don’t exceed ~60ms on average; tail tolerance up to 120ms during peak is acceptable.
- Throughput / Concurrency: our initial pilot will be ~300 qps (US) sustained; EU is expected ~120 qps. Peak concurrency across regions could hit ~900 qps during batch jobs.
- Streaming expectations: low jitter is important; we’ll want to do validation with a 15-minute synthetic load pattern to observe jitter and reconnect behaviors.
- Data residency: EU requests and logs must reside in EU-controlled infrastructure; we can accept pseudonymized logs if needed but prefer full auditability for compliance.

I’ll confirm with procurement next steps for contract cadence and will introduce Jane Park (compliance) on the thread if needed. For now, please send the SLO doc and any suggested routing options.

—Tom
Tom Li | Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
tom.li@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Appreciate the specifics, Tom — that helps a lot. Attached is the redwood-slos-matrix.pdf that maps our recommended SLO tiers to workload characteristics; I’ve highlighted the rows that match your targets. Quick notes: 

- We can meet p50/p95 targets for short prompts on our dedicated N1 profile with regional placement; p95 for longer contexts may be ~350–450ms depending on model and quantization choices.
- Streaming: we recommend using our streaming endpoints with client-side buffering set to 50ms to smooth jitter. We’ll run the 15-minute synthetic load test you requested.
- Regional routing/data residency: we support EU-only data plane for EU traffic and can provide separate audit logs per region. This will require a dedicated regional gateway for EU and a config change in the routing policy; no data will leave the EU gateway for EU-scoped requests.

Request: can you confirm expected sustained qps by region (US: 300, EU: 120, APAC: TBD) and whether logs can be pseudonymized if full audit logs are a blocker for the EU data plane cost? Once you confirm I’ll loop in Aditya for design validation and Rishi for procurement sizing.

Thanks — attaching the matrix and a rough routing sketch.

Attachments: redwood-slos-matrix.pdf, regional-routing-design.drawio

—Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Li <tom.li@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-16T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Hi Tom / Marissa — looping in infra/solutions notes based on the targets provided: 

1) Capacity & sizing
- For US (sustained 300 qps, peaks to 900): we recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscaled N1/N2 mixes and a hot standby buffer for spikes. Initial commit estimate: 8–12 GPU nodes depending on model family and batching.

2) Latency considerations
- Achieving p95 <= 250ms for short prompts is feasible with continuous batching tuned to low-latency mode and smaller micro-batches. We’ll need to know the typical prompt length and response length distribution to fine-tune kernel selections.

3) Streaming behavior
- Token-level latency target of ~60ms is realistic if we pin instances to low-latency configs and enable our fast path for attention kernels. We’ll instrument jitter metrics and provide a draft test harness for the 15-minute run.

4) Regional routing & residency
- EU data residency: we’ll deploy an EU control plane and EU-dedicated data plane. Logs can be delivered as full audit logs to an EU S3 bucket or pseudonymized before export; if Finova requires full auditability for compliance, we’ll mark that as a compliance requirement and scope pricing accordingly.

5) Questions for Finova:
- Can you share average prompt/response token counts and percentiles?
- Are session affinity / user stickiness required (i.e., same session pinned to same region)?
- Is APAC a hard requirement for go-live or considered in a later phase?

I’ll prepare a short design doc and a proposed sizing worksheet. Marissa — I’ll need the confirmed qps by region to finalize.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Solutions Architect
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Tom Li <tom.li@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Park <jane.park@finova.com>, Finova Procurement <procurement@finova.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing follow-up

Thanks — confirmed: US 300 qps sustained (peaks ~900), EU 120 qps sustained (peaks ~350), APAC pilot ~50 qps for now (not required for initial compliance).

Average tokens: prompts ~30 tokens median, responses ~45 tokens median; 90th percentile response length ~200 tokens. Session affinity: not required for our initial integration.

Compliance: Jane from Compliance on cc — we need full audit logs for EU data plane. Procurement will follow up on terms. Please send the design doc and sizing worksheet and we’ll schedule the 15-minute synthetic test window next week.

—Tom
